Let's break down each line as Nagiyev brags and Senya critiques the film industry.
'And what kind of banquet is it today?' Max aims this point right away: notice how Russian needs no word for "am", "is", or "are" in the present — placing the words side by side says it all.
'They finished filming a movie with me.' Nagiyev pushes back frankly with Senya, making his position completely clear.
'I have the lead role in it.' Nagiyev emphasizes this key touch in reply: "glavnoy" means "main" (from "glavnyy"), giving the line its exact edge.
'The comedy is truly very funny.' Nagiyev hands over this warning for Senya: notice how Russian needs no word for "am", "is", or "are" in the present — placing the words side by side says it all.
'Let's not get distracted from work.' Nagiyev fires back dryly as things stand, so Max knows he is not just making small talk.
'We prepare the salads and appetizers quickly.' Nagiyev frames one familiar word toward Senya: "zakuski" means "appetizer, snack" (from "zakuska"), giving the line its exact edge.

'Well, everything is clear with this movie.' Senya lays out the reaction in earnest: notice how Russian needs no word for "am", "is", or "are" in the present — placing the words side by side says it all.
'They filmed some nonsense again.' Senya weighs in steadily watching Nagiyev, keeping the focus on what actually matters here.
'And it will collect the whole box office.' Senya features one memorable expression at once: "soberyot" means "to collect" (from "sobrat"), giving the line its exact edge.

'Does anyone else think so?' Max brings that point around Senya: Russian keeps the exact word order of a normal statement here, turning it into a question for Senya purely through rising pitch at the end.
'This movie pays for itself before release.' Senya opens up openly with a shrug, without trying to dress up how he really feels.
